page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high clock speed family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, offering 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs via hyper-threading. The instance is allocated 128 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, and it features a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong capabilities in vector processing and data operations. Supported by AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets, the instance achieved top-quartile results in PassMark extended instructions (57136.8) and PassMark database operations (22550.06). It also registered an uncached memory read bandwidth of 209.21 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 269.5 GB/sec. Broader multi-core compute metrics, such as stress-ng (61243.12) and Geekbench multi-core (12682.0), placed consistently in the middle tier. Conversely, text generation metrics in CPU-based language model testing were weak, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated 64-vCPU configuration delivers high compute density for multi-threaded processes without the overhead of specialized coprocessors. Because local storage is absent, all storage operations depend on remote block storage, which requires appropriate architectural planning for high-IOPS applications. The instance is best suited for compute-bound batch processing, relational database operations, Clang compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data ingestion.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a high-clock-speed, compute-optimized virtual instance equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores via an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It includes 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, alongside a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in PassMark extended instructions and database operations, supported by AVX-512 extensions and 209.21 GB/sec in uncached memory read bandwidth. General multi-core processing, static web serving, and compression throughput align with median cloud averages, whereas CPU-based neural text generation is restricted. Consequently, the instance is targeted at compute-heavy parallel workloads, database services, and software compilation.
